extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental chemists, and critical readers/evaluators of chymical (early-chemistry) claims
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging the validity of chymical (alchemical/early-chemical) analyses and experimental claims: what counts as sufficient evidence, how experiments should be reported and interpreted, and how to avoid deception and equivocation. Focus is on experimental reproducibility, clarity of exposition, and the provenance of extracted substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide true and practicable methods for claimed separations
rubrics_metrics.description: He that would convince me of their truth, must first teach me some true and practicable way of separating Salt and Sulphur from Gold, Silver, and those many different sort of Stones...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that a body can be resolved into specific principles (e.g., salt, sulphur, mercury) require concrete, demonstrable, and repeatable procedures. Vague or purely verbal assertions are insufficient; the author must teach a practicable separation method so others can reproduce and verify the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate provenance and rule out contamination from reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: It will remain doubtful to a wary person, whether the Emergent Salt be that of the Gold it self; or of the Saline Bodies or Spirits employ'd to prepare it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that any substance obtained by analysis actually originates from the material under study rather than from the reagents, solvents, or apparatus used. Explain and control for interactions between reagents and the sample (examples: apparent 'salts' of metals that are actually mixtures with corrosive liquors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid asserting universal numbers/laws without broad empirical support
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not appear, that Three is precisely and Universally the Number of the Distinct Substances or Elements, whereinto mixt Bodies are resoluble by the Fire...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generalize from a small set of experiments to universal claims about nature (e.g., 'all compounds resolve into three principles'). Test across diverse materials and methods before proposing universal enumerations of elements/principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear, unambiguous, and consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: The unreasonable Liberty they give themselves of playing with Names at pleasure... they will now and then give divers things, one name; so they will oftentimes give one thing, many Names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define technical terms explicitly and use them consistently. Avoid giving one name to many different things or many names to one thing. Ambiguous terminology undermines the intelligibility and evaluability of experimental claims (examples cited: 'sulphur' and 'mercury' applied inconsistently).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish full methodological detail; avoid enigmatic obscurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whilst they affect that Ænigmatical obscurity with which they are wont to puzzle the Readers of their divulg'd Processes ... they leave wary persons much unsatisfy'd...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe experimental procedures, materials, vessels, heating, timings, and manipulations in sufficient detail so others can judge and reproduce the work. Avoid deliberate obscurity or mysterious phrasing that prevents independent assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include controls and guard against imposture; enable independent verification
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very easie for such as have some Skill, much craft, more boldness, and no Conscience, to impose upon them... I made my Experiment much more Slight, Short and Simple, ... to let them and others see how little is to be built upon the affirmation of those that are either unskillfull or unwary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments with appropriate controls, consider adversarial tests that detect fraud or artifacts, invite or enable independent replication, and use competent, skilled witnesses. Be alert to methods that can simulate claimed results by sleight or contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer observable evidence over appeals to authority or reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Though many profess'd Alchymists, and divers Persons of Quality have told me that they have made or seen the Mercury of Gold... yet I have been still apt to fear that either these persons have had a Design to deceive others; or have not had Skill and circumspection enough to keep themselves from being deceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat testimony and reputation with caution. Rely on reproducible, demonstrable results rather than authoritative assertion. Corroborate reports with independent experiments rather than accepting them on trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'element'/principle operationally (ingredient-based), not by usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements being call'd so in relation to the constituting of mixt Bodies, it should be upon the account of its Ingrediency, not of its use, that any thing should be affirmed or denyed to be an Element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify constituents based on their role in composing bodies (i.e., demonstrable ingrediency and separability), not on whether they are useful or active for human purposes. Provide criteria for what counts as an elementary constituent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish simple (elementary) from compounded corpuscles with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Even Corpuscles that are not of an Elementary but compounded Nature, may be of so durable a Texture, as to remain indissoluble in the ordinary Analysis that Chymists make of Bodies by the Fire...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that substances that appear indivisible under one method may be compound under another. Use multiple analytical techniques and seek evidence that purported 'elementary' corpuscles are not themselves composed of smaller parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental conditions and materials explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: I take then, of the filings of Copper, about a Drachme or two, of common sublimate, powder'd, the like Weight, and Sal Armoniack near about as much as of Sublimate; these three being well mingl'd together I put into a small Vial with a long neck... which (having first stopped it with Cotton) to avoid the Noxious Fumes, I approach by degrees to a competent Fire of well kindled coals...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete details (quantities, vessel types, closures, heat source, duration, observations during the run, and post‑treatment) so others can reproduce the procedure and evaluate possible artifacts (e.g., volatilization, sublimation, interaction with vessel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits of current evidence; withhold belief until proven
rubrics_metrics.description: I must take the Liberty to refrain from believing it, till the Chymists prove it, or give us intelligible and practicable Processes to performe what they pretend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the epistemic status of claims: distinguish conjecture from established fact, and refrain from dogmatic denial or acceptance when experiments are inconclusive. State what evidence would be required to convince a reasonable skeptic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple analytic agents/methods to reveal different components
rubrics_metrics.description: As Aqua Fortis, or Aqua Regis will make a Separation of colliquated Silver and Gold, though the Fire cannot; so there may be some Agent found out so subtile and so powerfull... as to be able to resolve them into those more simple ones...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different analytical reagents and methods (fire, corrosive menstruums, solvents, distillation, chemical reagents) can reveal different constituents. Apply several complementary techniques to test the robustness of a proposed decomposition and to detect otherwise hidden ingredients.
